learnings.title: Conditional essentiality is a real but modest, noisy signal — the achievable ceiling is low
learnings.detail: There is genuine within-gene conditional signal (which conditions stress a given gene), but it is intrinsically noisy: the best any model could possibly do is bounded by how well two biological replicates of the same experiment agree. That replicate-agreement ceiling is only NDCG@5 ~0.66 and within-gene Spearman ~0.39 on the within-organism task. This is an oracle/upper bound, not a target a model should be expected to approach — it reframes every downstream number: a method is doing well relative to ~0.66, not relative to 1.0.
learnings.evidence: Replicate noise floor (R-LOCK-4 oracle, retrieval_noise_floor over 23 orgs with adequate replicate design): NDCG@5 ~0.66 and Spearman ~0.39 — NDCG@5 runs 0-to-1 (1 = perfect top-of-list ranking), Spearman -1-to-+1 (0 = random). The oracle uses replicate A's fit as the prediction and replicate B's fit as ground truth, so it captures the irreducible biological noise floor. For contrast, the strong chem-kNN baseline reaches NDCG@5 0.485, i.e. roughly 73% of the way to a repeat experiment.
learnings.how_we_know: R-LOCK-4 defines a replicate oracle in harness.py that scores replicate-A-predicts-replicate-B; reported only for the 23 orgs with adequate replicate design so it is a fair per-org ceiling. Because it is measured the same way (NDCG@5/Spearman on the same eligible genes) as the models, it is directly comparable and establishes the scale.

learnings.title: The signal is gene-idiosyncratic and local — the population/cross-gene pattern carries ~0 within-gene signal
learnings.detail: Almost all of the usable conditional signal lives in each gene's own deviations from the bulk, not in any cross-gene population pattern. The 'population condition profile' (which conditions hurt most genes, gene-identity removed) is essentially useless for ranking an individual gene's conditions. This is why a global model that minimizes average error over ~54k genes captures the bulk and averages the idiosyncratic per-gene deviations away — they look like cross-gene noise to it — while a per-gene lookup preserves them.
learnings.evidence: chem-NULL (gene-blind population profile: predict every gene's fit at a cold condition as the train-gene MEAN at the chemically-nearest train condition) scores within-gene Spearman ~0.02 and NDCG@5 ~0.31-0.34 (0.3434 on the 23-org/3-seed headline) — near-random ranking despite being derived from real population structure. Any gene-aware method beats it: the deep model reaches NDCG@5 0.4319 and chem-kNN 0.4852.
learnings.how_we_know: chem-NULL is one of the three matched baselines scored on the identical eligible val gene set (denominator parity). Its ~0 within-gene Spearman directly demonstrates the population/cross-gene channel carries no within-gene ordering information, isolating the signal to per-gene deviations. Reinforced by the global-vs-local mechanism in synthesis section 4.

learnings.title: Cross-organism transfer of the conditional signal is ~0 — frozen protein embeddings carry no transferable cross-genome conditional response
learnings.detail: When entire genomes are held out (leave-genomes-out), the model's within-gene ordering of conditions is statistically indistinguishable from random. This is the pivotal negative that reframed the whole project from cross-organism to within-organism and from RMSE to per-gene ranking. Two causes: held-out organisms' genes sit far from any training gene in embedding space (no anchor), and the embedding is fitness-blind (it encodes sequence/structure/proteome-context, not stress response).
learnings.evidence: Cross-organism holdout (T-regime, multi_org_balanced split): within-gene Spearman ~0.045 vs a ~0.43 replicate noise floor — ~0.045 is near-random (0), ~10x below the ~0.43 ceiling. This co-existed with 'fine' pointwise error (RMSE ~0.50, MAE ~0.28), the exact trap RMSE hides. Homology cause quantified at 1.6 sigma (S1, H-HOMO-01: held-out-org genes far from train genes), corroborated by homology-bin RMSE rising ~0.40 (cosine<0.5) to ~0.55 (cosine>0.85). Fitness-blindness: ProteomeLM beat raw ESM-C by only RMSE ~0.006 (T5-C), so the proteome-contextual machinery added almost no conditional signal.
learnings.how_we_know: T1-T6 swept encoders/architectures/losses on a leave-genomes-out split (guardrails confirmed no split overlap); every arm sat at RMSE ~0.50 yet within-gene Spearman stayed ~0.045. The homology-bin RMSE breakdown and the ESM-C swap isolate the two causes. RMSE looking healthy while ranking is random is the durable lesson that low error can hide a useless model on a gene-mean-dominated target.

learnings.title: On the warm within-organism task, a chemistry-similarity kNN is a strong baseline that no learned global model beats
learnings.detail: chem-kNN — predict a gene's fit at a cold (unseen) condition from that same gene's own fit at its chemically-nearest train conditions — is the competitive gate, and every learned global model tested falls below it. This holds across encoders (fingerprint variants), objectives (pointwise and ranking losses), and capacities (linear bilinear MF up to a 2.5M-param deep model), and across both frozen sequence embeddings and learned fitness-aware gene representations. The deep model does clear the gene-blind floor, so it captures gene-specific structure — it just cannot beat local lookup.
learnings.evidence: 23-org/3-seed headline NDCG@5: chem-kNN gate 0.4852; best deep model (pointwise_huber) 0.4319 (gap ~-0.053); linear inductive-MF 0.4290; chem-NULL floor 0.3434. Promotion requires beating chem-kNN by >=~0.026 NDCG@5 with disjoint org->gene hierarchical bootstrap CIs — the model is BELOW the gate, not above it. Sweeps: R1 encoder (6 arms x 3 seeds), R-LOSS (MSE/Huber/RankNet/LambdaRank/ListMLE/ApproxNDCG, Huber best at 0.435), capacity (13k-param MF ~ 2.5M-param deep). All scored on identical eligible val genes (N=39,356 headline).
learnings.how_we_know: The locked harness enforces denominator parity (model and all baselines on the same eligible genes) and a strict disjoint-CI promotion gate. Independent sweeps of encoder, objective, and capacity all plateau at NDCG@5 ~0.42-0.44 below the 0.485 gate, and R-HYBRID (three learned fusions) converged on ~0 improvement — strong evidence the ceiling is real, not a single-design artifact.

learnings.title: The warm task is memorization-dominated — local lookup wins because the bottleneck is structural, not the embedding
learnings.detail: The useful deliverable ('rank a known gene's stressors in a known organism') is achievable at NDCG@5 ~0.485, but via memorization/lookup, not learning: reading each gene's own history and interpolating by chemistry similarity. Deep learning as configured adds nothing over it. Crucially the bottleneck is global-vs-local structure, not the embedding's fitness-blindness: a learned fitness-aware gene latent (linear-MF) does no better than the frozen sequence embedding, because the warm task is fundamentally about memorizing each gene's own history, which any GLOBAL representation compresses away.
learnings.evidence: Frozen sequence embedding (deep model) NDCG@5 ~0.42 vs learned fitness-aware latent (linear-MF) ~0.43 — swapping a fitness-blind rep for a fitness-aware one did NOT close the gap to kNN's 0.485; both lose. R-HYBRID confirmed: static z-ensemble gave only +0.008 over kNN (below the 0.026 gate), and three learned fusions (residual +0.0002, retrieval-augmented -0.0059, learned gating -0.0081) converged on ~0; learned gating settled at mean alpha ~0.46 but every unit of weight on the model HURT ('trust the lookup').
learnings.how_we_know: linear-MF is itself a fitness-aware-embedding experiment (free per-gene latents learned entirely from fitness data), so its failure to beat kNN isolates the bottleneck as global-vs-local rather than representation. R-HYBRID then showed even optimally combining global model + lookup extracts no promotable signal, and the learned gate's own weights point at the lookup. Together these say the warm task is memorization-dominated.

learnings.title: The negative is noise-robust — cleaner labels do not let the model overtake lookup
learnings.detail: The model-loses-to-kNN result is not an artifact of measurement noise. Stratifying eligible val genes by measurement confidence (Wetmore moderated t-statistic, abs_t), chem-kNN beats the deep model in every confidence quartile and at every per-cell |t| threshold — the model never overtakes lookup even on the cleanest-measured genes. Label noise does depress all measured performance and accounts for part of the model's deficit, but never enough to close it, and confidence-weighted training does not help.
learnings.evidence: R-CONF-DEC-001: chem-kNN > deep model in all 4 confidence quartiles and at every |t| threshold. Every method AND the replicate ceiling rise monotonically with confidence (ceiling 0.59 -> 0.83 from low to high confidence), confirming noise depresses measured numbers. The model-vs-ceiling gap narrows only 0.055 -> 0.040 across strata — narrowing but never closing. Confidence-weighted training changed NDCG@5 by ~-0.004 (no help).
learnings.how_we_know: abs_t (moderated t) is a per-cell measurement-confidence proxy; stratifying by it and re-scoring shows kNN's lead survives at high confidence, so the deficit is not label-noise-driven. The monotone rise of the ceiling with confidence proves noise is present and real, and the residual (structural, local-vs-global) gap that persists at high confidence proves cleaner labels would not fix the model.

learnings.title: The frozen embedding DOES carry transferable conditional signal — cold-gene generalization is a first positive
learnings.detail: The warm-split negative is a memorization gap, NOT an 'embeddings carry no signal' result. On the cold-gene split (unseen genes within known organisms), where chem-kNN vanishes because a gene has no own-history to look up, the global model (frozen embedding + chemistry) beats the only applicable baseline. This works because cross-GENE-within-organism transfer (place an unseen gene among the organism's seen genes, reuse the shared per-organism chemistry->fitness structure) is a much easier ask than the cross-ORGANISM transfer that failed at ~0.045.
learnings.evidence: Cold-gene, 23-org/3-seed, n=11,761 eligible cold val genes: chem-kNN/linear-MF coverage 0% (inapplicable — no own-gene history); chem-NULL gate NDCG@5 0.2447 / Spearman 0.0359; model NDCG@5 0.2748 / Spearman 0.0735; delta +0.0301 NDCG@5 / +0.0376 Spearman. Per-seed model NDCG@5 [0.2732, 0.2746, 0.2765] all disjoint above the constant 0.2447 gate; fast 3-org set reproduces the sign (+0.0271). HONESTY: on the primary metric the hierarchical CIs OVERLAP (model 0.2748 [0.2424,0.3179] vs gate 0.2447 [0.2118,0.2823]); only secondary Spearman is CI-disjoint. It is a directionally robust point-estimate win, not a strict disjoint-CI promotion, and against a weaker gate (chem-NULL) so it changes no headline number.
learnings.how_we_know: R-COLD-DEC-001 ran the diagnostic: chem-kNN's 0% coverage forces chem-NULL as the gate, and the model beats it consistently across all 3 seeds and reproduces on the fast set. The regime distinction (cross-gene-within-org vs cross-org) explains why the discouraging T-stage prior did not transfer. The overlapping primary-metric CI is reported honestly — it corrected an earlier Spearman-only 'CI-confirmed' read, which is why NDCG@5 is held primary.

learnings.title: Cofit leakage tripwire — never use feba.db's precomputed Cofit as a gene-gene edge on held-out splits
learnings.detail: feba.db ships a precomputed Cofit table (Pearson correlation between gene fitness profiles computed over ALL experiments, split-blind). Using it on any condition-holdout or cold-gene method is target leakage: the correlation spans the held-out val conditions, so a gene's top co-fitness neighbor's train profile reconstructs that gene's own held-out answer key. The rule: never read feba.db Cofit (or any all-experiment co-fitness matrix) into a cold-gene or condition-holdout method; co-fitness must be recomputed train-only, and on the cold-gene split a train-only co-fitness edge is undefined, so the frozen embedding is the only leakage-free gene-gene edge source there.
learnings.evidence: Smoking gun (round-2 evolutionary-search verification, Keio/Caulo/MR1): cofit-only NDCG@5 ~0.73-0.75, which EXCEEDS even the warm chem-kNN gate (~0.485) and approaches the replicate ceiling (~0.66) — physically impossible without a leak. Mechanism confirmed: the rank-1 cofit-neighbor's train profile correlates with the val gene's TRUE held-out profile at median r ~0.56 (63% of genes > 0.5). Inverted ablation confirms it: cofit-only outscores any fusion that includes it.
learnings.how_we_know: An impossibly-high NDCG@5 above the warm gate was the tripwire; the direct correlation between the neighbor's train profile and the val gene's held-out truth (median r ~0.56) is the mechanistic proof of the leak, and the inverted ablation (adding cofit only ever helps, never hurts, and cofit-alone beats everything) confirms it is answer-key contamination rather than signal. This is why honest gene-axis methods (GENE-NW) reduce to the R-COLD embedding signal instead of adding new information.
